title: Determination of Underground Water Quality, the Main Source of Drinking Water, in a Village Area in North-Eastern Romania, Based on “In Situ”  Physical-Chemical Analysis
content: In the historical context of the evolution of water sources, from wells, rivers and lakes to the construction of water filtration and treatment plants starting from the 19th century, the concept of “clean water” has acquired a precise definition, based on parameters such as pH, redox potential and salinity. Today, public authorities consider drinking water safe when it meets strictly defined standards for human consumption. Starting from this framework, this study aims to analyze the water quality from wells in a rural area in northwestern Romania, where they represent the main source of water for the local population. 80 wells were evaluated, focusing on the total dissolved solids (TDS) pa-rameter, used as the main indicator of water quality. Since TDS is not standardized at the national level, the values recommended by the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) were used. In addition, parameters such as dissolved oxygen (DO), ox-ygen saturation, salinity, conductivity, redox potential and pH were analyzed. For comparison, the values of these parameters were also measured for the water from the public network of the municipalities of Iasi and Botosani, as well as for various brands of bottled water. The results of the study highlight significant water quality problems in rural areas, especially in terms of microbiological contamination and high nitrate levels, highlighting the need for urgent measures to improve infrastructure and water treat-ment systems. These findings contribute to a better understanding of the challenges related to ensuring drinking water in rural communities and provide a basis for de-veloping effective public policies in water resources management.
